subject: Information Theory
title: Error Correction in Space
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Error Correction in Space.

hook.text: Voyager 2 transmits at 20 watts from 12 billion miles away. The signal arriving at Earth is trillions of times weaker.

buildup.text: Deep-space signals are incredibly faint. Without error correction, most received bits would be garbage.

discovery.text: NASA uses concatenated codes: an inner convolutional code plus an outer Reed-Solomon code. Double protection.

twist.text: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter uses turbo codes, pushing data rates 10× higher than older missions at the same power.

climax.text: Every stunning image of Saturn's rings and Pluto's heart traveled billions of miles error-free thanks to coding theory.

punchline.text: Billions of miles. Trillions of times weaker. Zero errors.

quiz.question: How does NASA protect deep-space data?
